responses.title: Button 7 Makes the Turret Say No
story: Before this change, the box only reacted to the four arrow keys. Button 7 on the remote did nothing. The new line teaches the box one more trick: when it hears button 7, it shakes its head no.

Here is how it works. The box listens for the remote all the time. When a button is pressed, it reads a number called a command code. Button 7 has the code 0x7, and the sketch gives that number the nickname cmd7.

The new line is a case inside a switch. A switch is a list of 'if you hear this, do that' rules. The new rule says: if the key is cmd7, run shakeHeadNo(3) and then stop checking the list. The 3 means three shakes. The break is the stop sign.
The other changed lines only swapped empty marker comments for blank lines. The computer ignores those, so the box acts the same there.

steps.label: Name the key
steps.detail: The sketch gives the code 0x7 the nickname cmd7, so button 7 is easy to read in the code.

steps.label: Wait for a key
steps.detail: The box checks over and over whether the remote sent something.

steps.label: Read the code
steps.detail: The switch looks at the command number that arrived and compares it to its list of rules.

steps.label: New rule
steps.detail: If the number matches cmd7, the box runs shakeHeadNo(3), which is the new line.

steps.label: Shake no
steps.detail: The turret turns right, stops, turns left, stops, and repeats that three times.

responses.metaphor: The switch is like a mail sorter: each key code goes into its own slot, and slot 7 now has a job.
responses.watch_for: Press button 7 on the remote and watch the turret turn left and right three times, like shaking its head no.
